object_description: freely oriented volumes with punctual built fronts responding to the rural village grain
geometry_property: three levels concentrated in one building
design_condition: the morphology, scale and location of the volumes interact with the rural character of the site, their freely oriented fronts responding to the punctual framework of the rebuilt village

positive: The morphology, scale and location interact with the rural character of the site
The freely oriented built fronts respond to the punctual framework of the village
Public spaces are defined by the expansions of the path from the passage to square, schoolyard and car park
The space freed between school, covered courtyard, church and barn holds the outdoor programme
It is naturally divided into a sub-space for the children classes and another for the primary classes
A play area, parking and bus drop-off complete the outdoor facilities
The village square sits on an axis connecting the lower village, the passage and the new school
The site maintains pleasant permeability, enhancing views of the great valley landscape
The landscape project strikes a good balance between passage, sharing and planted spaces
The class programme is concentrated in one building over three levels
The after-school reception has its own entrance facing the square and public access
Another entrance linked to the schoolyard serves the classes above
A central distribution space is pleasantly lit, notably by a skylight open to all levels
A generous covered courtyard is judiciously offered
The facade expression and the modesty of the exterior arrangements reinforce the rural anchoring
The structure presents great rationality for both vertical and horizontal load transmission
The cement screed gives good thermal inertia
The cold roof reduces the heated volume and creates a thermal buffer zone
The jury highlights the quality of the location of the buildings and the scale of the exterior spaces
negative: The articulation of the project with the cemetery is insufficient
The opportunity to improve or pool the parking lot is missed
The village square and playground areas seem undersized
The qualities of the covered courtyard are lost with the proposed extension
The extension height greatly reduces the quality of sunlight in the schoolyard
Implementation in wood should be adapted to constructive reality, degrading the fineness of the facade lines
The complicated geometry of the central circulation strongly overlaps the rest of the building
This makes the use of wood more difficult for fire protection
The central stairwell cannot be extended to the basement without restrictive measures
